chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, raising it (to the Imam), said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Three (people) do not receive the greeting (of peace): the one walking with the funeral, the one walking to the Friday prayer, and the one in the bathhouse.'

key_terms.الْمَاشِي: the walker / one who is walking

ai.seo_question: Who are the three people who do not receive greetings according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates three specific contexts where the greeting of 'As-salam' is withheld to preserve ritual focus or social decorum: accompanying a funeral procession, walking to the Friday congregational prayer, and being inside a bathhouse. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on contextual mindfulness (khushu') in daily interactions, distinguishing between casual social greetings and those reserved for moments of spiritual or physical transition.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, raising it, said,
‘It was so that Abu Abdullahasws was saying: ‘Three (persons) would not be greeting (السَّلَامُ) – the walker along with the funeral, and the walker to the Friday Salāt, and in the bath house’.
en.sarwar: 11. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn in a marfu’ manner from an Imam who has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) would say, ‘Three kinds of people do not offer greetings: one walking in funeral procession, one walking to attend Friday prayer and in the bathing places.’”
